lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The Leafs stopped wobbling before the building could start buzzing with doubt - Anthony Stolarz stood tall in a 2-1 win over the Islanders, and that matters because Toronto is 1-1-0, first in the Atlantic Division, with a little air in its lungs again. After the flat 3-2 loss to Montreal, this was the kind of game that steadies a room: Easton Cowan brought the spark, the young legs, the bite on the forecheck, and Stolarz gave the club the backbone with a calm, veteran hand in net. One win does not erase the opening stumble, but it does change the mood. Next comes Ottawa on Saturday night, and the Leafs had better bring the same pace, because division position is earned, not inherited.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The bill came due in Toronto, and the club is left staring at the same old problem - not enough offense, not enough margin, not enough wins. Mark Shapiro backed Vladimir Guerrero Jr. after his contract comments, a public show of faith that matters because the Blue Jays need their biggest star to become their most reliable bat again. The final line - 79-83, fifth in the AL East - tells the whole story without drama. This wasn't a club undone by one bad week; it was undone by ordinary nights that stayed ordinary too long. Guerrero remains the central question, and the front office's answer sounds simple: keep him, fix him, and add more thunder around him. Now comes the hard part - turning postmortems into power, and making the winter count.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The first crackle of camp in Quebec City has come from the same place championship teams always do: the new star and the old cornerstone finding their footing together. Kawhi Leonard has already turned heads with his shooting touch and pace in camp, but he has not yet joined live scrimmages as Toronto eases him in - a caution that feels wise for a club with bigger plans than October vanity. Scottie Barnes, meanwhile, is carrying himself like a man ready to sharpen every edge of his game, and the talk around young guards Walter and Murray-Boyles says the depth chart is not settled yet. Toronto opens preseason Saturday against Miami, then the real measuring stick arrives October 21 against Chicago. For now, the watchword is fit: Leonard's ramp-up, Barnes' next leap, and which young legs force their way into the rotation.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The Commanders have life again, and it came the hard way - by surviving a 33-31 edge over Seattle and turning a week of doubt into a week of noise. Marcus Mariota's 183-yard, three-touchdown night powered the upset while Jayden Daniels returned to practice in limited fashion, a reminder that Washington's season is still very much under construction. At 1-2, third in the NFC East and a game back, they're not buried, but they've got work to do. Daniels remains the story - limited Wednesday, still uncertain for Sunday - and his elbow is the hinge this team swings on. Now comes the true test: Sunday in London against the Colts, with Daniels' status and Washington's 1-2 start hanging in the balance.

the_latest.dek: The win gave Washington its first victory of the season and kept a narrow path open in a crowded NFC East race. It also showed the Commanders can survive injuries and still beat quality opponents when the defense creates chances and the offense finishes them.

article.title: Stolarz Leads Leafs Past Islanders
paragraphs: Anthony Stolarz made 26 saves and Easton Cowan had a goal and an assist as the Leafs beat the Islanders 2-1 last night. Colton Sissons also scored, and Toronto gets the Senators next Saturday at 7 p.m. on Sportsnet.

That gives the Leafs a 1-1-0 start, with a cleaner look in goal and some early pop from Cowan. The Blue Jays are still in offseason mode after a season full of hard questions, the Raptors open preseason against the Heat on Saturday before their regular-season opener against the Bulls on Oct. 21, and the Commanders face the Colts on Sunday morning while Jayden Daniels remains uncertain after returning to practice in limited fashion.
